first_impression.reaction: We haven't picked a country yet and Greece is on the list, so I Googled it. I expected 'say I do under the Aegean sun' and got a sorting rule instead: 'the right one depends less on the view than on three practical questions: how many guests you are inviting, which kind of ceremony you want, and how those guests will travel.' Then 'A caldera terrace in Oia suits 40 people.' We're 60 to 90, so that one line just changed my shortlist. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Curfews, minimum nights and rain plans are rarely published, so have them confirmed in writing before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: This is the stuff that turns into a surprise invoice. Telling me what isn't known is more convincing than pretending everything is.

journey.section: How to compare Greece wedding venues like for like
journey.quote: Exclusive use is the field most often misread.
journey.reaction: Exactly the kind of fine print I'd get caught on. The Grace versus Canaves comparison makes it concrete. Lawyer brain approves.

journey.section: Greece wedding venues at a glance (table)
journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state it on its official pages.
journey.reaction: The table is the bit I'd screenshot for James. Lots of 'Not published' cells, but at least it's honest about the gaps.

journey.quote: A ceremony in the Fira garden and drinks on an Oia terrace means a cross-island transfer, so keep both at one hotel where you can.
journey.reaction: Insider detail. Nobody on Instagram mentions this, and it's precisely our grandparents problem.

journey.quote: Every wedding needs a wedding planner involved at least three months before the date.
journey.reaction: Useful to know some venues require a planner. Makes the case for one without a sales pitch.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms each Corfu venue's house rules and seated numbers in writing.
journey.reaction: By the fifth region I'd read a version of this line after every section. Got the message the first time. Starts to feel like a template.

journey.quote: Ikos Aria and Sani Resort plan around 30 guests.
journey.reaction: This is under the rooms question, but earlier Sani's 30 was its ceremony space, not rooms. Are these guest rooms or event numbers? I'd want that clear before I rule them out.

journey.quote: Since 30 March 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System has been fully deployed for non-EU travellers, passport control may involve long waits, and the airport advises arriving at least 2.5 hours before departure.
journey.reaction: Didn't know this. Half our guests are flying in, so this goes straight into the welcome-drinks timing.

journey.quote: passengers usually carry their own luggage up and down stairs.
journey.reaction: My nan on a ferry ramp with a suitcase. This is why we'd hire someone. Honest and slightly terrifying.

journey.quote: It is a 2.5-hour drive from Athens International Airport, so plan a daylight coach and a rest day before any event.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off on a venue that would otherwise be top of my Pinterest board.

journey.section: Getting legally married in Greece as Australians
journey.quote: Whether a chapel ceremony is legally binding for non-Orthodox couples is confirmed couple by couple.
journey.reaction: The checklist of questions to put to the municipality is good, but this line leaves me thinking we might just marry at home first. Clear enough to have that conversation tonight.

journey.section: Shortlist your Greek venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Goes at the hidden-costs fear, and 'quoting in AUD' helps with currency. Still doesn't say who is physically there on the day if something goes wrong.

unanswered_questions: Is our Wedded Advisor, or someone you are accountable for, physically in Greece on the day, or do you hand over to a local planner we've never met?
Is there a real wedding you've planned at one of these 20 venues, with the venue and date, that I can look at?
For a guest list of 60 to 90 with half flying in, which two or three of these would you actually shortlist?
Do you organise the guest ferries and transfers, or just advise on them?
would_share_with: James (partner): the at-a-glance table and the Santorini capacity point, because it rules out a caldera terrace for us
Mum and Dad (contributing): the getting-there section, especially the airport wait times and ferry luggage stairs
Our parents again: the legal questions list, so they understand why we might marry at home first

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest count and the venues you have in mind, and [speak with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary).
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and it asks for exactly what I can give. But I'd want to see one real Greek wedding you've done and read one more post before I hand over our details.

top_3_changes: Cut most of the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms ... in writing' closers after each region; say it once strongly and let the venue detail do the work.
Fix the rooms FAQ so Sani Resort's 30 (event space) and Ikos Aria's 30 (accommodation) aren't lumped together as the same thing.
Say plainly who is on the ground on the wedding day and whether you book the transfers, since the transport section raises that worry and doesn't answer it.

open_questions.question: The Sani/Ikos '30 guests' line in the rooms FAQ may be a factual conflation, not just a reader confusion. Worth a quick editor check?
